real_capture_first500.txt / real_capture_multi_date_cusip.txt -- provenance
(W5c, 2026-09-18)
============================================================================

Captured with a single real HTTP GET (1 of the 2 requests allowed for this
source under the W5c constraints):

    GET https://www.sec.gov/files/data/fails-deliver-data/cnsfails202608b.zip
    User-Agent: GRID/1.0 (aniksrobot@gmail.com)
    HTTP/1.1 200 OK  (Server: nginx, X-AH-Environment: prod)
    Captured: 2026-09-18
    Zip size: 1,393,881 bytes; single member cnsfails202608b.txt,
    uncompressed 3,874,330 bytes, 61,550 data rows (settlement dates
    2026-08-17 through 2026-08-31, i.e. the "second half of August 2026"
    file -- consistent with the documented ~15th-of-next-month publication
    lag for second-half files, relative to a 2026-09-18 capture date).

3,874,330 bytes is over the ~2 MB threshold in the task brief, so per
instructions the extracted ZIP member is NOT stored whole. Two small real
(not constructed) slices were kept instead, both taken verbatim from the
one real decoded file above -- no values were invented:

  - real_capture_first500.txt: header + the first 500 data rows of the
    real file, unmodified. All 500 rows happen to share settlement date
    2026-08-17 (each date block in the real file runs ~5,000-6,000 rows,
    so any contiguous 500-row prefix stays within one date).
  - real_capture_multi_date_cusip.txt: header + every row (11 of them) for
    one real CUSIP (Y4000A102 / symbol HQ / "HORIZON QUANTUM HLDGS LTD
    SHS") that recurs across all 11 settlement dates present in the file
    (2026-08-17 .. 2026-08-31), with 11 different QUANTITY (FAILS) values
    (373, 2245, 71, 1258, 3348, 145601, 9502, 16511, 26351, 3294, 179).
    This slice exists specifically to test, on real data, that the puller
    stores each settlement date's balance independently rather than
    summing/overwriting across dates -- see
    `test_real_fixture_same_cusip_across_dates_not_summed` in
    tests/test_source_sec_ftd.py.

Trailer lines ("Trailer record count ..." / "Trailer total quantity of
shares ...") from the real file were deliberately dropped from both
slices -- they are not part of either sample's row count and would only
be parsed as (harmlessly skipped, non-fatal) malformed 1-field rows by
`parse_ftd_file`, same as in the original file.

Format check against the documented layout (SETTLEMENT DATE|CUSIP|
SYMBOL|QUANTITY (FAILS)|DESCRIPTION|PRICE): the real file matches exactly
-- pipe-delimited, 6 fields, 8-digit settlement date, integer quantity,
header row present. No discrepancy observed here (contrast with the FINRA
short-volume capture -- see the sibling NOTE.txt in
tests/fixtures/sources/finra_short_volume/).

Per-request budget used for this source: 1 of 2 allowed. No retry was
attempted (the response was a 200, not a failure).
